neutral_facts.value: The accused and the deceased had a sudden fight over a stolen pigeon. The co-accused, who had a rod, struck the deceased on the head with the rod, causing his death. The accused and the co-accused then disposed of the deceased's body in a canal. The incident occurred after consuming liquor, and there was no pre-meditation. The scuffle happened in the heat of passion due to a sudden quarrel. The deceased did not respond after the blow, and the body was moved to the canal.

appeal_history.value: Trial court: Convicted under Sections 302/34 and 201 IPC; High Court: Modified conviction to Section 304 Part-I/34 IPC and maintained conviction under Section 201 IPC; Supreme Court: Modified conviction to Section 304 Part-II/34 IPC and maintained conviction under Section 201 IPC

quotes.text: The conviction of the appellant is modified from the one under Section 304 Part-I/34 IPC to the one under Section 304 Part-II/34 IPC. The appellant is hereby sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of seven years and the fine of Rs.10,000/- imposed by the High Court is maintained. Further, conviction of the appellant for the offence under Section 201 IPC and sentence of three years’ rigorous imprisonment and the fine of Rs.500/- are also maintained.

prosecution_argument.value: The State of Punjab argued that the High Court's conviction of the appellant under Section 304 Part-I IPC was incorrect and that there were no grounds to interfere with the High Court's judgment. The State also contended that the case law relied on by the appellant was distinguishable on facts and could not be applied to the case at hand.

quotes.text: It is further contended that the case law which is relied on by the appellant is distinguishable on facts and cannot be applied to the facts of the case on hand.

defence_argument.value: The appellant's counsel argued that there was no intention to kill the deceased, the scuffle was a sudden fight in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel, and it was not a pre-meditated act. They submitted that the conviction under Section 304 Part-I IPC should be modified to Section 304 Part-II IPC, citing the precedent of Uday Singh v. State of U.P. and Shahajan Ali & Ors. v. State of Maharashtra & Ors.

quotes.text: It is submitted that there was no intention at all on the part of the appellant-accused to kill the deceased. It is submitted that the appellant, co-accused and deceased had consumed liquor and on the ground that the deceased had stolen pigeon of appellant Kala Singh, scuffle took place between deceased Shamber Singh and appellant Kala Singh. It is submitted that at that point of time, the co-accused Kehar Singh gave one rod blow on the head of the deceased Shamber Singh which resulted into his death. It is submitted that scuffle had taken place on the spur of the moment and that sudden fight had taken place in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel. It was not a pre-meditated act and there was no intention at all to kill the deceased.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that if there was no intention to cause death or such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, the conviction under Section 304 Part-I IPC should be modified to Section 304 Part-II IPC.

quotes.text: It is clear from the evidence on record that the scuffle had taken place on the spur of the moment and a sudden fight had taken place in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel. It was not a pre-meditated one and as there was no intention on the part of the appellant and co-accused either to cause death or cause such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, the High Court ought not to have convicted the appellant for the offence under Section 304 Part-I IPC.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the Supreme Court found that the scuffle was a sudden fight in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel, there was no pre-meditation, and no intention to cause death or such bodily injury as is likely to cause death. Therefore, the conviction under Section 304 Part-I IPC was modified to Section 304 Part-II IPC, while maintaining the conviction under Section 201 IPC.

quotes.text: It is clear from the evidence on record that the scuffle had taken place on the spur of the moment and a sudden fight had taken place in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel. It was not a pre-meditated one and as there was no intention on the part of the appellant and co-accused either to cause death or cause such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, the High Court ought not to have convicted the appellant for the offence under Section 304 Part-I IPC.

other_sentence_order.value: The appellant was sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of seven years and a fine of Rs.10,000/- was imposed. Additionally, the conviction under Section 201 IPC and a sentence of three years’ rigorous imprisonment with a fine of Rs.500/- were maintained.
